  • CDS FAPE Fiscal Presentation
  • Child Outcomes Survey Data Collection
10/15/2025 This presentation provided an overview of the ongoing transition of Child Find and Free Appropriate Public Education (FAPE) responsibilities from Child Development Services (CDS) to School Administrative Units (SAUs). Presenters from the Maine Department of Education shared updates on state-level efforts to strengthen collaborative partnerships between childcare programs and SAUs, ensuring seamless coordination and continued support for children with disabilities across early learning settings. YouTube
  • Owners and Directors of Licensed Childcare Programs
10/22/2025 This Cohort 2 presentation provided information on Developmental Delay as an eligibility category for preschool aged children, including identification and assessment processes, reminders about adverse impact statements, reevaluations based on age, and, with regard to the IEP process, developmental needs, goals, and services. YouTube
  • Evaluation, Eligibility, and the IEP under Developmental Delay
11/12/2025 This Cohort 2 presentation provided information on Early Intervention (EI-Part C of IDEA) and the transition to Preschool Special Education (ECSE) by the 3rd birthday. Includes information on differences between EI and ECSE, timelines, eligibility and IEP meetings. YouTube
  • Early Intervention to Early Childhood Special Education Part B to Part C
11/18/2025 This Cohort 2 presentation provided information about Free Appropriate Public Education (FAPE) and Least Restrictive Environment (LRE) in the mixed delivery system and included information about the continuum of placement options, and LRE codes. YouTube
  • Least Restrictive Environment LRE for Cohort 2
11/20/2025 This presentation was developed to share information about steps and practices involved in participating in future Cohort 3 and 4 Transitions to FAPE in SAUs. YouTube
  • Cohort 3 & 4 Presentation: FAPE Transition
12/3/2025 This Cohort 2 meeting included a review of previous presentations on Partnerships and an opportunity for attendees to discuss progress on working within the mixed delivery system. Strategies were presented as well as tips and tools. YouTube
  • Cohort 2 Partnerships Review
12/17/2025 Cohort 2 Meeting and the Offer of a FAPE in Public Schools. This meeting covered the requirements for public education offerings, children's access, services, and the IEP/ISP.  YouTube
  • FAPE in Public Schools for Preschool-Aged Children Presentation
  • FAPE in Public Schools Guidance Document 12/15/2025
1/14/2026 Cohort 2 Meeting sharing information on Early Childhood Education and support for the youngest learners in early care and education settings.  YouTube
  • Youngest Learners in Early Care and Education Settings
1/28/2026 The meeting focused on exclusionary discipline policies and behavior management strategies in early childhood education, with presenters reviewing Maine's regulations around suspensions, expulsions, and restraint/seclusion for preschool-aged children. SAUs discussed behavior challenges and supportive resources. YouTube
  • Discussion of Maine's Early Childhood Discipline Regulations
2/4/2026 The meeting focused on introducing a new early childhood special education monitoring tool within the Grants for Maine system. The session included an overview of the tool's functionality, including how to navigate the system, enter expenditure data, and document high-cost placements. The tool will be used for fiscal oversight of early childhood special education funds, with reports due 30 days after each quarter. YouTube
  • Grants4ME Presentation
2/11/2026 Cohort 3 and 4 Informational Meeting served as a welcome session focusing on the transition of early childhood special education services from Child Development Services (CDS) to school districts. The leadership team highlighted the importance of this transition, emphasizing its potential to have a significant long-term impact on students. The team introduced key members from various departments, including early childhood special education consultants, coordinators, and CDS leadership, who will support the transition.  YouTube
  • Cohort 3 & 4 Welcome Presentation
2/11/2026 Cohorts 1-4 Informational Meeting focused on updates and plans for the transition of early childhood special education services to school districts across Maine. Topics included the new early childhood special education webpage, upcoming professional development sessions, the CDS Support and Service Hub model, and the Early Learning team's upcoming sessions and solution labs to support districts in developing mixed-delivery systems. YouTube
  • Cohorts 1-4 Informational Meeting Presentation
2/25/2026 This Cohort 1-4 Informational Meeting shared follow-up information on specific behavior supports to prevent and intervene with challenging behaviors. Models such as Multi-tiered Systems of Support (MTSS) and Positive Behavior Intervention Systems (PBIS) can also support early childhood to prevent challenging behaviors, teach replacement behaviors, and develop specific interventions when necessary. Resources, trainings, and an early childhood-specific framework were described YouTube
  • Cohort 1-4 Informational Meeting Presentation on Challenging Behavior
2/25/2026 School Finance presentation on Early Childhood Special Education funding and building a needs-based budget. Additionally, information was shared on reporting requirements, enrollment data reporting, uploading into Grants4ME, account codes, billing MaineCare, and State Agency Clients.  YouTube
  • Budgets and Funding in Early Childhood Special Education
3/11/2026 The Cohort 1-4 presentation on the Itinerant Model of Early Childhood Special Education included an introduction to the terms and a rationale for this delivery system of special education services. Guest Speaker Dr. Laurie Dinnebeil shared how the model began and the practices key to its implementation.  YouTube
  • Itinerant Service Delivery Overview
3/13/2026 A presentation to the Penobscot River Educational Partnership (PREP) Pre-K teachers that describes how early childhood classrooms support all learners, including children with disabilities, and what the transition of FAPE to school districts means for Pre-K programs.   
  • Supporting Children in Early Childhood Classrooms
3/25/2026 A presentation about EnGiNE, the state's learning management system and communication platform, that describes how to access the latest information about early childhood special education topics. Join the ECSE portal (includes detailed instructions) and complete the feedback form.  YouTube
  • EnGiNE in Early Childhood Special Education
  • Registration Family Connections and Three Year Olds
4/6/2026 Information in this session was provided on Chapter 676 and its relationship to schools participating in the Transition of FAPE in Early Childhood Special Education from CDS to SAUs   

  • Chapter 676: What SAUs Need to Know & Do
4/15/2026

Information was shared about topics:

Capitalizing Assets-fiscal presentation on asset capitalization, purchasing requirements, four steps of the needs assessment, preapproval process and waiver. 

Data in Early Childhood Special Education- a review of data collections, methods, and presentation of results.

Signing up for EnGiNE to receive communications, reminders and updates for Early Childhood Special Education topics.

 YouTube

  • Early Childhood Special Education Funding: Capitalizing Assets

  • Data Presentation for SAUs
5/6/2026 AEYC Presentation on the transition to FAPE by SAUs YouTube
  • Transition and Q&A for Maine Association for Education of the Young Child 
5/6/2026 Cohort Informational Session: Top 10 Questions Answered for Delivery of FAPE in Early Childhood Special Education  
  • Top 10 Questions for the Delivery of FAPE in Early Childhood Settings
5/20/2026 Cohort 1-4 Presentation: End of the Year Celebration. A review of the steps and actions taken by SAUs in the Cohorts, and partnership activities conducted by the state to support the Transition of FAPE to SAUs. YouTube
  • End of School Year 2026 Recognition and Celebration
6/17/2026 Cohort Summer Office Hours Presentation: Transition Activities of Early Intervention. Updates to activities, rules, procedures, including Extended Early Intervention procedures and policies. YouTube
  • Early Intervention Transition Session 1
6/18/2026 Presentation on Itinerant Model of Early Childhood Special Education. This presentation was offered to practitioners working in early intervention and early childhood special education within CDS to orient them to the model's foundational elements, practices, and principles. Includes information about Extended Part C. YouTube
  • Introduction to the Itinerant Model of Early Childhood Special Education for CDS
6/22/2026 Session 2 of the Transition Activities of Early Intervention. Reviewed potential scenarios of age and setting preferences, Extended Part C.  YouTube
  • Early Intervention Transition Session 2
7/15/2026 Summer Office Hours    
8/19/2026 Summer Office Hours: Child Outcomes Summary Training- This presentation included a review of the Child Outcomes Summary Process for IEP teams and its data submission requirements. Links to supportive forms and presentation of techniques to accomplish the process were presented.  YouTube
  • Child Outcomes Summary Process Review and Data Submission Requirements
9/2/2026 Summer Office Hours: Early Childhood Special Education Enrollment and Early Childhood Special Education Least Restrictive Environment and Placement Codes. This presentation describes the data submission methods schools use (e.g., Synergy, Infinite Campus, etc.) to share data with the DoE, how to access reports in Connect and NEO for Early Childhood. A follow up presentation was made to frame Least Restrictive Environment, Placement and Setting, access to typical peers and presented scenarios to use each of the nine Placement Codes. YouTube
  • Early Childhood Special Education Enrollment
  • Early Childhood Special Education Least Restrictive Environment and Placement Codes
